captions.detailed: A matte black bicycle front-end assembly featuring a straight unicrown steel commuter fork, a headtube, a riser stem, and wide flat handlebars. The fork has integrated fender/rack mounts at its dropouts and a straight steerer tube. The flat handlebars sweep back slightly and terminate in flared ergonomic hand grips. The entire steering assembly (fork, stem, and handlebars) can rotate continuously relative to the fixed headtube.
captions.instruction: Generate a CadQuery model of a city commuter bicycle front assembly, featuring a straight-blade unicrown steel fork, a headtube, a riser stem, and flat handlebars with ergonomic grips. Ensure the steering column is articulated to rotate continuously relative to the headtube, and apply a matte black finish to all primary components.
captions.factory: Construct the assembly by first modeling the fixed headtube as a central cylinder. Create the steering column as a child part containing the fork (using cylinders for the blades and steerer tube, and boxes for the dropouts), the riser stem (constructed from combined cylinders and boxes), and the handlebars (swept cylinders with flared grip ends). Define a continuous revolute joint between the headtube and the steering column along the Z-axis to enable realistic steering rotation.
